verdict.rationale: AnythingLLM's own docs describe a local-first design: it runs entirely on the user's computer, 'no data leaving your device', and meeting transcription uses 'No cloud processing'. That inherently keeps data away from training pipelines when local models are used. However, the evidence never states a no-training policy or offers a training opt-out, and hosted or cloud-LLM setups ('Just bring an LLM API Key') send data to third-party providers. missing for 10: explicit no-training policy or opt-out control, coverage of training protections when cloud LLM providers or vendor hosting are used, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Every document becomes part of your agent's knowledge base with no data leaving your device.
A private AI assistant that runs entirely on your computer.
No bots joining your meeting. No cloud processing.
